items.q: What got cheap, and what did not?
items.a: Writing code sped up (GPT-5 / Gemini 3 in the room). **Deciding what to build did not.** That is Ng's product-management bottleneck in lecture form.

items.q: What happened to the eng:PM ratio?
items.a: Old Valley talk: one PM keeps **4–8 engineers** busy. Ng is seeing **2:1 or 1:1** — or **one human who is both**. Take the numbers with salt. The direction does not wander.
**No.** Ideas outnumber builders. A failed weekend is cheap. Do not harm others. Then go.

items.q: What is Moroney's first move when someone says 'build an agent'?
items.a: Ask **why** until the sentence has **no AI and no agent**. Sales example: they wanted an agent. They needed salespeople **20% more efficient** at pre-call homework.

items.q: What four steps make an agent?
items.a: **Intent → plan (with tools) → execute → reflect.** If the result misses intent, replan. A toolkit is not an agent.

items.q: What is the mortgage test for vibe coding?
items.a: A house you can service is **good debt**. Shoes on a credit card are not. Prompted spaghetti you cannot debug is the credit card.
Say the dull true sentence. **Text-to-video is next-frame prediction.** Consistency bugs stop being magic. You become useful.

items.q: What is Small AI vs Big AI?
items.a: **Big AI:** hosted frontier, AGI race, privacy risk for Hollywood/law/medicine. **Small AI:** self-hosted open weights on a phone or one GPU. Next year's **7B ≈ last year's 300B.** Sooner bubble on Big; later on Small. Learn to ship value on both.
**No.** It is hours. You are what you **measure**. Output, not 9-to-9 six days.
